trans.sense: enclosed structure where cigarettes, magazines, etc are sold
enclosed structure where cigarettes, magazines, etc are sold

examples.text: I remember that one time I went to the kiosk next door to buy condoms, it was raining, she appeared.
examples.ref: 2021, Pedro Mairal, The Woman from Uruguay, Bloomsbury Publishing, →ISBN, page 143:

glosses: A small enclosed structure, often freestanding, open on one side or with a window, used as a booth to sell newspapers, cigarettes, etc.

examples.text: Not only has the infamous upgrade gone by the wayside, but cashiers at fast-food restaurants are becoming increasingly uncommon. McDonald's started rolling out ordering kiosks at its US locations in 2015, and the chain hasn't looked back since: by 2020, most of its 14,000 locations will have kiosks installed.
examples.ref: 2018 July 26, Hollis Johnson, “We tried the kiosks that analysts say could help McDonald's win back $2.7 billion in sales. Here's the verdict.”, in Business Insider:

glosses: A similar but unattended stand for the automatic dispensing of tickets, etc; an e-kiosk.
